message.content:
The volume \(V\) of a cone is given by

\[
V = \frac{1}{3}\,\pi\,r^{2}\,h
\]

where  
\(r = 3\;\text{cm}\) (radius) and  
\(h = 5\;\text{cm}\) (height).

Plugging in the numbers:

\[
\begin{aligned}
V &= \frac{1}{3}\,\pi\,(3\,\text{cm})^{2}\,(5\,\text{cm}) \\
  &= \frac{1}{3}\,\pi\,(9\,\text{cm}^{2})\,(5\,\text{cm}) \\
  &= \frac{1}{3}\,\pi\,(45\,\text{cm}^{3}) \\
  &= 15\,\pi\,\text{cm}^{3}
\end{aligned}
\]

Using \(\pi \approx 3.14159\):

\[
V \approx 15 \times 3.14159 \;\text{cm}^{3} \approx 47.12385\;\text{cm}^{3}
\]

So the volume of the cone is approximately **47.12 cm³** (exactly \(15\pi\;\text{cm}^{3}\)).
